source_text: hanc fuisse redditam Dei munere Abrahae et Sarrae senio confectis emortuisque corporibus ut asseram si possum, ad opus diaboli pertinere, quod Deum videam interdum conferre pro munere
pass_a_gloss: This to-have-been redditam of-God munere Abrahae and Sarrae senio confectis emortuisque bodies so-that/as asseram if i-am-able, to work of-the-devil pertinere, that/which God sees interdum conferre for munere.
pass_b_english: [Sexual desire] was restored by God’s gift to Abraham and Sarah when old age had worn them out and their bodies were as good as dead.
Let him say, if he can, that something he sees God sometimes bestow as a gift belongs to the devil’s work.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
